intended_object: The homeomorphism Proj(ℬ) ≃ₜ Proj(𝒜) between the underlying topological spaces of the projective spectra, induced by an isomorphism of ℕ-graded rings 𝒜 ≅ ℬ, given as a pair of mutually inverse graded ring maps f, g. It sends a relevant homogeneous prime p to f⁻¹(p). Inferred from the docstring and the module doc.
explanation:
The forward map is `ProjectiveSpectrum.comapFun f`, which pulls back a homogeneous prime along f, and the inverse map is `comapFun g`. The two maps are inverse to each other because `comap g ∘ comap f = comap (f ∘ g) = id`, and the same holds in the other order. Each map is continuous because it is the underlying function of Mathlib's continuous map `ProjectiveSpectrum.comap`. The condition comap needs, ℬ₊ ≤ map f 𝒜₊ (the irrelevant ideal of ℬ lies inside the image of the irrelevant ideal of 𝒜), follows from f and g being inverse to each other. So this is the standard homeomorphism of projective spectra induced by a graded ring isomorphism.

The generality is natural: Mathlib defines `ProjectiveSpectrum` only for ℕ-graded rings, and the two rings may live in independent universes. Taking an inverse pair of maps instead of a bundled graded ring equivalence is equivalent; I found no such bundled equivalence type in the Mathlib directories I searched. I also found no Mathlib declaration that gives this homeomorphism.
